newsitem.title: CHINA: Rockwell, China sign MOU on electronics.
newsitem.headline: Rockwell, China sign MOU on electronics.

text.p: Rockwell International Corp of the United States has signed an agreement with China's Ministry of Electronics to study possible cooperation in electronics, a company official said on Thursday.
The memorandum of understanding, signed on Wednesday, would eventually help boost Rockwell's current US$50 million investment in China, company chairman Donald Beall told a news briefing.
"We think this will lead to greater cooperation between the Chinese government and several of Rockwell's areas," he added.
Rockwell's major business areas are automation, semiconductor systems, avionics and communications and automotive components.
The agreement will initially explore cooperation in modem and wireless communications with the aim of setting up "design centres" across China to help the electronics industry, Beall said.
Rockwell has four joint ventures in China. Three produce auto components, including axles for heavy duty trucks and highway vehicles, as well as window regulators for cars.

The firm earlier in 1997 also formed a joint venture with Shanghai Avionics Co and the Shanghai Broadcast Equipment Factory to produce commercial global positioning receivers, Beall said. It said the venture would begin sales later this year.

The company is also competing to be chosen to provide the avionics for the 100-seater airliner to be developed by China, Singapore and a European consortium, but Beall said he was unsure when the project partners would make a decision.
Aviation Industries of China holds 46 percent of the $2.1 billion venture. The other partners are Aero International Asia, a part of Airbus Industrie, and Singapore Technologies Aerospace.
The venture is targeted to deliver its first airliner by 2001.
